name: Documentation bloat
peeve: Instructions growing through rationale, duplicated claims, correction notes and comments that explain readable code.
look_for: a doc edit that adds a paragraph; sentences explaining why a rule exists, what a section is about, or how it came to be written
owner: web-tools CLAUDE.md (before adding to a doc, ask whether another document owns it)

name: Fix the sentence, add no note
peeve: Correct a living document by fixing the sentence: the smallest edit that removes the error, with no new paragraph and no 'formerly', 'corrected' or 'superseded' note.
look_for: an error fix that grows the file; a sentence recording what the text used to say
owner: home CLAUDE.md (status markers retired: fix the sentence)

name: Unexplained jargon
peeve: Familiarity with a local or specialized term being assumed of the reader. An established technical term can still need an introduction.
look_for: a coinage or insider term (pin, hunk, emitter, the estate, guide delimiter) used without a definition

name: Dramatic prose
peeve: Slogans, posturing, emphatic absolutes and sentences that sound profound while saying little.
look_for: 'it does one thing', 'is the floor', 'held to', 'carries weight', 'does the work', 'deliberately', 'never' used for emphasis; a sentence that sounds wise and says little

name: Vague writing
peeve: Claims a reader cannot check, unnamed subjects and pronouns whose referents the reader has to recover.
look_for: 'a file here', 'some cases', 'it is complicated'; a sentence that cannot be checked; two replies that disagree silently

name: Name the referent
peeve: Introduce the subject before referring to it, and name the referent each time: no bare 'this', 'it', 'that one file'; each bullet must stand alone.
look_for: a pronoun or definite phrase whose referent is several sentences back; a bullet that only makes sense after the one before

name: Em dashes
peeve: Dashes used to join ideas in prose. The existing entry also covers en dashes and double hyphens used for that purpose.
look_for: an em dash, en dash or double hyphen between clauses
owner: docs/QUALIFIED-WRITING.md (no em dashes); home tools/lint-conventions.py catches em dashes and double hyphens in home only

name: Say a thing once
peeve: Say a thing once: one owner per statement, linked from elsewhere, never restated in a second file, a header and its list, or a table and its caption.
look_for: the same claim in two documents, or in a heading and the line under it

name: Missing attribution
peeve: A borrowed idea presented as the project's own view, or analysis presented as an authoritative verdict. Attribution identifies whose idea or judgment the reader is seeing and links its source.
look_for: 'the panel's verdict', 'our theory' for a borrowed idea; a summary of a source where a link to it would do

name: Term loading
peeve: Giving ordinary or specialized terms a private meaning, or assuming the reader shares meanings drawn from unspecified context.
look_for: a familiar word used for a special local concept; an unexplained coined, metaphorical or insider term; a meaning imported from another discussion or file without introducing it; competing names that leave the referent unclear

name: Retired words
peeve: Do not use the words the owner has retired: register in a coined sense, carry as a verb for what a file holds, carrier for a data file, and tray.
look_for: a guidance register, a file that carries a list, a data carrier, a tray of material

name: One name per thing
peeve: Give one thing one name everywhere: file name, label and title match, with no aliases, exception tables or number suffixes.
look_for: a file called one thing and labelled another; 'v2', 'new', or a second name for an old concept

name: Literal names
peeve: Name things for what they are, not by metaphor or vague umbrella.
look_for: a figurative label (rack, a spicy name) or a catch-all group label (authored) where a plain descriptive one exists

name: Missing context
peeve: Summaries that assume the reader followed the session, already understands the subject or authored pasted material.
look_for: a summary that starts mid-thought, relies on earlier turns, or credits pasted text to the owner

name: Rambling replies
peeve: Buried conclusions, side issues and detail that distracts from the owner's question.
look_for: a wall of text; a reply that ranges across several subjects; the conclusion at the bottom

name: Subtle veering
peeve: Quietly taking the work in a different direction from the owner's proposal, leaving the owner to discover the departure later.
look_for: a change in scope, approach, output or framing that is not called out when the direction changes; explaining the departure only after the owner notices

name: Stay on the main issue
peeve: Stay on the owner's main issue; do not drift into possibilities, side topics, your own terminology or immaterial discrepancies.
look_for: paragraphs on a side issue; a rounding difference treated as a finding

name: Shallow defense
peeve: Treating an available rationale, measurement or precedent as sufficient to dismiss the owner's challenge. A choice can have justification and still be bad. Entertain the criticism, examine the tradeoff and revise the choice when warranted.
look_for: a rationale or measurement offered as if it settles whether a choice is good; a challenged choice repeated without considering the criticism; weak reasons used to dismiss an idea

name: Extra setup
peeve: Delivery that makes the owner download short copyable text, assemble patch fragments or save and configure a script intended to run directly in the PowerShell ISE.
look_for: a SendUserFile card for a short text or a script

name: Unclear status
peeve: Closings or PR descriptions that misstate what is finished, open, merged or verified on the current commit.
look_for: 'done' with next steps listed; 'clean exit' with open items; the same marker restated after each CI event

name: Lazy questions
peeve: Asking the owner to inspect available evidence, settle a question the assistant can resolve or approve an already agreed next step.
look_for: 'Shall I proceed?' or 'Want me to...?' on a path already agreed; a question whose answer is in the repo

name: Raw options
peeve: Handing the owner choices without the assessment and recommendation needed to decide.
look_for: a list of options without a recommendation; a question with no context to answer it
owner: home CLAUDE.md; the portable ask-question-guard hook refuses only the AskUserQuestion tool, not a menu written in prose

name: Missing links
peeve: References without usable links, render links that miss the changed view and links that stop short of the named item.
look_for: a viewable change with no render link; a link that loads blank or lands on the wrong view; a standalone page link where the app route renders it (framed pages excepted, per home CLAUDE.md)
owner: docs/CONVERSATION.md (npm run showing picks the link)

name: Link what you mention
peeve: Link every file, PR, session or page you mention.
look_for: a path or PR number in prose without a link

name: Untested claims
peeve: Reporting an inferred result as demonstrated, handing over an unexamined screenshot or proposing a fix before checking the cause.
look_for: 'should work'; a screenshot sent without comment on what it shows; asking the owner to run the test

name: Three options for a visual choice
peeve: For an open visual choice, show about three options as screenshots and recommend one.
look_for: a single guess, or options described in words

name: State at each stop
peeve: At each stopping point, volunteer what was done, what is open, whether it has landed on main, and whether it is ready to wrap and merge.
look_for: a reply that ends without saying whether the work is finished or merged

name: Shown versus inferred
peeve: Separate what was demonstrated from what was inferred from reading code, and hedge unverified claims; do not call an assessment completed work.
look_for: 'works' for something only read; 'all' or 'every' without having checked

name: Resolve open questions
peeve: Resolve open questions wherever the evidence allows; do not hand the owner new items to review.
look_for: an open-questions list that grew; items the session could have settled

name: Wording diff before commit
peeve: Show proposed wording for a doc or skill as a diff in chat, with context and a link to the file, before committing it.
look_for: a doc or skill edit committed without the owner seeing the wording
owner: web-tools .githooks/commit-msg via skills/hooks/commit-consent.py (modified Markdown only); skills/hooks/warn-governing-docs.sh at edit time

name: Finish in this session
peeve: Finish what can be finished in this session; do not defer it to a later session, a follow-up, or someone else.
look_for: 'left for a follow-up', 'out of scope', 'not mine to land' for work the session could do

name: No unrequested tasks
peeve: Do not file a tracker task unless the owner asks for one.
look_for: a new task file the owner did not endorse

name: Reinventing the wheel
peeve: Adding a mechanism, category or separate interface when an existing one serves the job. One-off interfaces bypass the app shell, file viewer or shared component without a reason the existing interface cannot serve.
look_for: a new folder, registry, name or layer next to one that already exists; a workaround mechanism for a simple problem

name: Reduce when cleaning up
peeve: When cleaning up, reduce rather than add; do not add rules, guards or documentation for a single incident or a hypothetical, and do not widen the scope (orchestration, fan-outs) without being asked.
look_for: a guard script for one mistake; a fan-out nobody asked for; a cleanup that added lines
owner: web-tools CLAUDE.md (wary of improvements for hypothetical problems)

name: Read the guide first
peeve: Before acting or asserting what exists, read the relevant skill or style guide and check the latest main, other repos and open branches.
look_for: a page built without html-style; 'there is no X' from a stale or shallow clone

name: Micromanaged handoffs
peeve: Handoff prompts that prescribe detailed steps, solutions or option rankings beyond the goal and necessary context.
look_for: a step-by-step handoff where an outcome and constraints would suffice; instructions that leave the receiving session little room to exercise judgment

name: No unasked deletions
peeve: Do not propose deleting a feature, page or branch unless its removal was clearly intended.
look_for: a cleanup that removes working features

name: Unfinished work
peeve: Leaving feasible work for another session, stopping before an authorized merge or declaring a tool failure after trying one route.
look_for: stopping at 'ready for your review' after being told to merge; a PR left with a conflict

name: PR babysitting
peeve: Timed check-ins and redundant status messages about unchanged PR or CI state. A new failure, review or merge can warrant a message.
look_for: a scheduled CI check-in; the same status repeated after each event; redundant PR or CI status messages when the state has not changed
owner: docs/CONVERSATION.md (PR events); the portable send-later guard refuses only send_later

name: PR body matches final state
peeve: Keep the PR description aligned with the final state, and confirm CI on the final commit.
look_for: a PR body describing an earlier plan; 'green' claimed for an earlier head

name: Try another route
peeve: When a tool or PR route fails, try another route before reporting it blocked.
look_for: 'could not create the PR' after one failed call

name: Explanatory prose
peeve: Pages spending space explaining their purpose or controls when the structure and labels could make the purpose clear.
look_for: a sentence on the page saying what the page or a section is for

name: No repeats or dead weight
peeve: Remove what repeats or carries no use: a header that restates the tab, count badges on tabs, duplicate buttons, filters and pills nobody needs.
look_for: a heading echoing the selected tab; a count on every tab; two controls for one action

name: Wasted space
peeve: Repeated headings and controls, unnecessary boxes and padding, or an artificially narrow reading column. Comfortable text size and contrast remain requirements.
look_for: generous padding, a card inside a card, a rounded box inside a full-bleed viewer; small or pale text bought for compactness

name: Reuse app components
peeve: Reuse the app's components and conventions (viewer, swipe deck, tooltip kits, toggles, tabs), and show content in the app's own viewer, keeping the GitHub link a view carries.
look_for: a one-off control where a kit exists; a link out where the viewer could show the file
owner: skills/html-style/SKILL.md; docs/APP.md (every new view carries its GitHub link)

name: Works at phone width
peeve: Make every view work at phone width: no sideways page scroll, tables scroll inside their container under sticky headers, controls neither wrap nor shift, inputs at 16px.
look_for: horizontal page overflow at 390px; a control row that wraps; layout that moves when a count gains a digit
owner: web-tools page-measures (npm run shot --measure) reports sideways overflow only; the rest is a reader's check

name: Full width
peeve: Use the full width; never narrow text to a reading column or a centered corridor.
look_for: max-w-prose, max-w-2xl to 4xl, container mx-auto, a ch cap
owner: skills/html-style/SKILL.md (rule 3); the reading-column hook refuses class caps at edit time, and misses caps in CSS or written through the shell

name: Stat cards
peeve: Tiles that put a label over a big number without the comparison, baseline or movement needed to interpret the figure.
look_for: stats, stat-value, a KPI grid

name: Built tooltips only
peeve: Tooltips: never a fact in a title attribute, and never a daisyUI tooltip, data-tip or question-mark cursor; use the title-tip or panel-tip kit, a few words, light, closing on tap.
look_for: title=, data-tip, cursor-help, a dark tooltip, a tooltip paragraph
owner: skills/html-style/SKILL.md (rule 11); npm run stranded-titles lists facts parked in a title, advisory

name: Wordy labels
peeve: Labels that spend several words on an action a plain word or recognizable icon could express.
look_for: 'Open the guide', 'Copy to stage'; a book icon followed by the word Read

name: Heavy styling
peeve: Dark tooltips and overlays, heavy outlines and saturated controls. Tooltips use the app components and remain brief, light and dismissible on touch.
look_for: black fills or pills, outlined buttons inside an outlined card, dark text on saturated red

name: Inline expanders
peeve: Accordions and nesting that hide list structure or interrupt reading. The list and separate detail panel used for Peeves is the preferred example.
look_for: sections stacked down the page; collapse and expand used to hide structure

name: Views inside the app
peeve: Show new views inside the app shell at their route, and put findings in data the app displays, not in a standalone page or a Markdown report.
look_for: a standalone HTML page for something that belongs in a view; findings left only in a .md file

name: Internal clutter
peeve: Opaque identifiers used as labels, export dates or internal state shown without a reader purpose, and warnings for ordinary conditions.
look_for: a hash or id shown as a label; 'you' in page copy; a warning for an expected state

name: Instant and undoable
peeve: Interactions respond at once and can be undone: no hover delay or long animation, tooltips dismiss, there is a way to back out, destructive clicks confirm or undo.
look_for: a delay before highlight; a click that deletes with no undo

name: Crafted first drafts
peeve: Give a first draft craft: study the app's best existing views before designing, and never ship a stock template.
look_for: a generic prototype layout; the dashboard template's tiles and hero

name: Aligned icons
peeve: Align icons, pins and highlights with the line of text beside them, and check it in a screenshot.
look_for: an icon sitting a pixel or two high or low against its label

name: Hard-coded data
peeve: Information embedded in presentation or scripts, a Markdown table parsed to recover structured rows, or stored values already available from git or the app.
look_for: values typed into HTML or Python; a script that parses Markdown into a table; a stored date git already has

name: PowerShell for the ISE
peeve: PowerShell for the owner pastes into the ISE and runs with F5: no param block, nothing to save, no comments beyond the skill's one # @file line, delivered as a link on the branch.
look_for: a param() block, comment headers, instructions to save and run a .ps1

name: Few short comments
peeve: Keep code comments short and few.
look_for: long comment blocks explaining code that reads plainly

name: One drop-in patch
peeve: Offer a patch as one larger drop-in block that says where it goes, or as a link on the branch; never several small patches.
look_for: two or three fragments to paste into one file

name: Links land on the item
peeve: A link lands on the specific item it names, and its text says what that item is.
look_for: a link that opens a tab or a document top instead of the item; the same generic link text repeated; a link whose text does not name its target

name: Forced line breaks
peeve: Source paragraphs broken across lines at an arbitrary width. Paragraphs remain continuous; the renderer controls visual wrapping.
look_for: a paragraph broken across lines at a fixed width in a .md file or a PR body

name: Percussive negation and contrast
peeve: Repeated denials of outcomes the reader never expected, or repeated contrasts that manufacture an alternative to reject. Percussive negation and percussive contrast spend attention on those rejected alternatives. A necessary comparison or correction can still state a contrast.
look_for: 'draws no underline', 'adds no claim', 'names no file', 'open no new ones', 'nothing opens it'; several in one passage; excludes have, be and there is; repeated 'not X, but Y' contrasts; rejecting an alternative the reader never raised

name: Compatibility clutter
peeve: Aliases and fallbacks kept without a named dependency that requires them. An outside caller can justify compatibility. A migration names the concrete completion step that allows the old form to be removed.
look_for: 'still resolves' or 'keeps a saved link working' with no outside reference found; an alias or legacy fallback whose consumers are all in the estate; a removal date with no completion step

name: List synonyms
peeve: Calling a list a ledger, census, catalog or similar term and expecting the word to establish the list's meaning. The defined uses of registry and stream retain their existing exceptions.
look_for: the news ledger, a skills catalog, the census test, a branch survey; a list term implying that a list is complete, append-only or authoritative without saying so
owner: docs/registries.md (registries and streams); home CLAUDE.md (name the subject, not the genre)
